clue.text: Programme includes student's first multiplication aid

indicators.note: includes means the programme word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a timetable is a programme or schedule of events

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word student's is used

explanation.surface: A school programme features a pupil's first tool for learning multiplication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts S, the first letter of 'student's', inside TIMETABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Children learn arithmetic by reciting these number grids, so they are a learning aid for multiplying.

clue.text: Record knock by opener for Essex

parts.note: a tap is a light knock

indicators.note: opener for means the first letter of the word Essex is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket report on a knock by an Essex opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'knock' is an innings and an 'opener' a first batsman; Essex is an English county side. Here they mean TAP and the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something is to capture it on magnetic media, as with a cassette or video.

clue.text: Handle work of art after staff

indicators.note: after places the art word behind the staffing word

parts.note: to man something is to staff it
an oeuvre is a work, or body of work, of an artist

explanation.surface: Someone handles an artwork after the stick it was hung on.
explanation.definitionFit: To manoeuvre something is to steer or handle it skilfully, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sounds like Arab leader with broken nose — point and show disbelief

indicators.note: Sounds like tells us to take the pronunciation of the Arab leader word

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab chief, often said to rhyme with bake

indicators.note: broken means the letters of nose are rearranged

parts.note: a head is a point of land jutting into the sea, as in Beachy Head

explanation.surface: An Arab chief with a broken nose points and shrugs off a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving the head from side to side is the gesture for doubt or refusal, an idiom.

clue.text: In question, investment after a short time

indicators.note: after places the investment word behind the time pieces

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a stake is money invested in a venture

explanation.surface: An investment is queried shortly after it was made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at stake is the very matter being risked or debated, so it is under consideration.

clue.text: Protracted dance, or friendly ball?

parts.note: something protracted is drawn out or long
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A drawn-out dance, or perhaps a sociable party with music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' seems to continue the dance theme, but it is a cricket delivery: a long hop pitches short and bounces up invitingly, easy for the batsman to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a poor, short-pitched delivery is generous to the batsman, a playful description of a bad bowling error.

clue.text: Hereditary, in part? Correct

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the word Hereditary is used, its inner letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is partly inherited, answered with a nod.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct and revise it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Navigator, one at home on second part of 8?

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis ..., the Elizabethan seafarer who sailed round the world

definitions.text: one at home on second part of 8?
definitions.meaning: the second word of 8 down is a liquid; a male duck lives on ponds and lakes

explanation.surface: A seafarer who feels most at home afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: Entry 8 is TREAD WATER, so its second part is WATER, where a male duck lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan explorer bears this surname, and a male duck is called by the same word.

clue.text: We dart and tear all over the place, but fail to make progress!

indicators.note: all over the place suggests letters scattered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: People rush and charge about frantically yet get nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping afloat without moving forward is an idiom for staying in place without advancing.

clue.text: Mountain-dweller also described by the old man

indicators.note: described by means drawn round, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: pa is an informal word for one's father, the old man
and means also or in addition

explanation.surface: Dad also tells of someone who lives high in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant black-and-white bear lives in mountain bamboo forests of China, an example of a mountain animal.

clue.text: Acts I deny working for cartel

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone denies their acts were carried out on behalf of a cartel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of businesses combining to control prices, a kind of commercial association.

clue.text: Enid treated, end not exactly established

indicators.note: treated means the letters of the name are processed into a new order

parts.note: to terminate is to end

explanation.surface: Enid received medical care, and her end remains uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague or not fixed precisely is undetermined, a synonym for not definitely settled.

clue.text: Heard I was hard? Nonsense

indicators.note: Heard means the words I was are taken as spoken, sounding like an organ of sight plus was

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYEWAS
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone hears that they were said to be tough and calls it rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is idle talk meant to deceive, a colloquial word for rubbish.

clue.text: Fear of onset of darkness? Study needed

indicators.note: onset of means the beginning letter of the word darkness

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Is a fear of nightfall something that needs research?
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Advocate anaesthetic? Old issue

parts.note: to back a cause is to advocate it
something more anaesthetic makes you more numb, hence number

explanation.surface: A doctor recommends a painkiller, but it is outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as 'more numb', a comparative adjective, the job an anaesthetic does.
explanation.definitionFit: A past edition of a magazine or newspaper is an earlier issue, the publishing term.

clue.text: Further loan

definitions.meaning: to further something is to promote or move it forward
money paid ahead of time, such as a sum lent against wages

explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it means to further; as a noun it is a sum lent or paid early.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of moving forward: pushing a cause on, or money given before it is due.

clue.text: Bone tossed initially into Spanish dish

indicators.note: into means the opening letter is placed inside the rice dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish from Valencia

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word tossed

explanation.surface: A bone is thrown carelessly into a pan of Spanish rice.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is a small bone at the front of the knee joint, its anatomical name.

clue.text: Fall in love, then become disillusioned

definitions.meaning: to give one's affections away to someone

explanation.surface: Someone falls for a person, then grows disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is usually 'lose one's heart'; the second the plain idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving away your affections and losing your nerve are both idioms built on the same phrase.

clue.text: Noisy celebration in joint's at an end

parts.note: the knee is a leg joint; with the 's it gives knees
up means finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A rowdy party at which a sore joint has finally given out.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: This British colloquialism describes a lively, boisterous party, often with singing and dancing.

clue.text: Foul-mouthed supporter, English, supporting old hand

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the following pieces beneath, holding up the first

parts.note: a pro is a professional or old hand
a fan is a supporter of a team

explanation.surface: An English football fan swears at a veteran player.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane language is irreverent and coarse, so a profane speaker uses obscenities.

clue.text: Envisage opponent tackling reserve by end of game

indicators.note: tackling means the opponent word grips the reserve word inside it

parts.note: a foe is an opponent

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word game

explanation.surface: A player imagines a rival tackling a substitute near the final whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to predict or picture the future, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Female, Italian head, in good health

parts.note: It is an abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A woman from Italy who leads a team is in fine shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitness is the condition of being physically sound, a synonym for wellbeing.

clue.text: Article taken from grubby relative

indicators.note: taken from means the article is removed from the grubby word

parts.note: grubby means dirty or unclean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grubby family member's belongings are confiscated.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, an example of a relative.

clue.text: Appeal of tea room

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: The attraction of a tearoom.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is attractiveness or pleasing allure, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Bird — I check on unfamiliar sort

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the first pieces after the rearranged ones
unfamiliar means the letters of sort appear in a strange new order

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher checks on a bird of a strange kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest living bird, flightless and native to Africa, an example.

clue.text: Try to listen

definitions.meaning: a judge tries a case, sitting in court to judge it
to take in sounds with the ears

explanation.walkthrough: A court hears a case when it tries it.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges hear cases in court, and to hear is also simply to perceive sound.

clue.text: Draughts, perhaps, made bar go uncomfortable

indicators.note: uncomfortable suggests letters ill at ease, moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Cold air currents made a bar unpleasant to sit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughts' suggests cold air, but it is the board game, called checkers in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts, called checkers in America, is an example of a game played on a chequered board.

clue.text: Saw a duke decline

parts.note: to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: Someone watched an aristocrat refuse an invitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense; it is a noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional proverb or maxim, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Peculiar piano seat

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An odd stool for a pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' looks like a piano stool, but it means the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the buttocks, the part one sits on, so seat is a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Young landlord enclosing second bulletin

indicators.note: enclosing means the first pieces wrap round the next one

parts.note: new means young or recent
a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: A new landlord sends tenants a second bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landlord' gives LETTER, one who lets property, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsletter is a regular printed report circulated to members, a kind of bulletin.
